evidence.excerpt: Industrial sites often run several ICS protocols concurrently; a single anomaly may manifest in traffic from multiple protocols or only one. This paper compares six score aggregation strategies—maximum, mean, product, Dempster-Shafer combination, learned linear combination, and a voting threshold rule—for combining per-protocol anomaly scores from Modbus, DNP3, and EtherNet/IP detectors deployed simultaneously on the same network segment. A testbed with all three protocol stacks was operated for 45 days, and 18 multi-protocol and single-protocol attack scenarios were injected over a 10-day evaluation period. The learned linear combination, trained on a 5-day clean holdout with synthetic contamination, achieved the highest balanced accuracy (0.91) but required labelled data for weight estimation. The Dempster-Shafer rule achieved 0.88 without labelled data. The maximum rule performed consistently below 0.80. Results provide concrete guidance for operators designing multi-sensor detection pipelines.
